README documents CLI usage only. It has no REST API or library docs. The `--json` flag loads site data and is not an API.

corrected.one_liner: Open-source (MIT) Python command-line tool that checks whether a username exists across 400+ social networks and sites.
corrected.auth_notes: No API and no authentication. It is a local CLI that makes unauthenticated requests to the target sites. There are no vendor credentials.
corrected.access_notes: No hosted or public API. You install it yourself (pipx/pip/uv, Docker, dnf) and run it locally, which is free. The README does not mention a library API or a hosted service.
corrected.blocker: There is no API. A toolkit would have to run the CLI as a subprocess. A community MCP server (Burnsedia/sherlock-mcp) does this with one search_username tool, but Glama lists it as outdated and it is not verified as maintained. It needs a runtime that can execute the CLI. Results depend on per-site checks and can include false positives and negatives. Searching people by username raises privacy and ToS concerns. Under a strict hosted-API definition this is no_public_api, so switch it to blocked if you require a hosted API.
